Subject: GPU SKU allocation: memory tiling & OOM mitigation for NovumAI reserve

Team —

NovumAI's CTO sent over a more detailed token profile and a sample of long-context queries (attached). They're asking us to lock SKU mix for their Dedicated reserve (12-month, committed). They want deterministic latency under 120ms p50 for their interactive product and can tolerate some background batch jobs for embeddings.

High-level ask: recommend an H100/A100/L4 split that minimizes monthly cost while avoiding OOM tail events for queries up to 120k tokens (typical long-context slices are 40–80k). Also include a short mitigation plan for peak OOMs and a fallback policy (which model variant to route to when memory pressure spikes).

Important constraints:
- Customer will pin a single model family for the reserve (currently planning LlamaX-70B fp16/8-bit variants).
- On-prem access not an option; US-region hosted Dedicated pool only.
- They want to use KV caching aggressively for session affinity.

I've attached: novumai-query-profile.csv (sample request lengths) and an initial tiling-simulation.pdf (quick sim I ran locally).

Can you take ownership of the SKU recommendation and ops fallthrough? Kim — please validate memory ceiling assumptions and how much headroom H100 buys vs A100 for the LlamaX long-context mixed-precision pathway. Ben — please prepare a quick cost delta (tokens/month) estimate for each SKU mix and a suggested canary rollout plan.

Thanks,
Jasmine

Thanks for the packet, Jas. Quick notes after skimming the profile + running a few micro-tests on the LlamaX-70B fp16 path:

- Memory characteristics: with fp16 KV cache and typical attention tiling we see ~0.9–1.1x working memory on H100 vs A100 for the same sequence length. The interesting delta is that H100's larger HBM and improved memory coalescing reduces out-of-core pressure for very long KV chains (60k+ tokens) — effectively reducing transient OOM events by a nontrivial amount.
- A100 (80GB) in 1:1 mapping will hit memory ceilings for worst-case 120k tokens unless we aggressively shard or force tiling; that increases CPU orchestration complexity and latency risk.
- L4 is excellent for short interactive paths and for embeddings (cost-effective), but it cannot hold the full KV state for 40–80k sessions; we'd need to partition sessions across L4 nodes or rely on hybrid routing back to larger memory hosts.

Operational mitigation suggestions:
1) Default reserve pool: hybrid mix with H100s for long-session primaries and A100s as mid-tier failover. Example starting mix for a 50-slot pool: 6x H100, 24x A100, 20x L4 burst nodes (L4s sized for embeddings and short-chat).
2) Soft OOM policy: automatic session spill-to-disk (slow path) with token-limited degradation message to user; prefer fallback to A100 or to a lower-rank model variant depending on latency budget.
3) Aggressive KV prefix caching: reserve ~15% of capacity exclusively for hot-session KV (reduces repeated loads).

I'll attach a quick spreadsheet with memory curves later today. Needed from Ben: expected concurrent sessions (p50/p95) and monthly token budget so I can convert to slot-hours and run a cost comparison.

—Kim

- Concurrent sessions: p50 ~ 1,200, p95 ~ 3,100. These are for the interactive product only; embeddings batch jobs (nightly) add a separate throughput load but can be run on burst nodes.
- Token distribution: the attached csv is accurate — we see a heavy tail with ~12% of requests > 40k tokens and a small subset (~1.6%) > 90k.
- SLA priority: interactive latency trumps cost for p50; p95 can incur higher tail latency if required. We prefer that p50 stays below 120ms and that p95 stays reasonable (<300ms) wherever possible.

If H100 meaningfully reduces transient OOMs for the 60–120k range, we prefer to keep a healthy H100 presence even if it costs a bit more. For canary we can start with 10% of traffic on H100s.

Thanks — alignment looks good. Final recommendations for the deal deck and ops runbook (to include in the renewal/commit SOW):

1) Reserve composition (recommended initial):
- H100: 20% of committed GPU slots (dedicated for long-session primaries for p50-sensitive traffic)
- A100: 50% of slots (bulk capacity, lower cost per-token for steady-state long requests with tiling enabled)
- L4: 30% of slots (cheap burst capacity for embeddings and short interactions; route user sessions here only when length < 8k tokens)

Rationale: this mix balances p50 latency needs with cost. H100s handle the very long KV-chains and reduce OOM tail risk; A100s carry the bulk with tiling; L4s are cost-savers for non-KV workloads.

2) Canary + rollout policy:
- Canary: 10% traffic to H100 on day-1; monitor OOMs, p50/p95 latency, KV cache hit rate for 72 hours.
- Autoscaling rules: prefer vertical slot addition in A100 tier for steady throughput; trigger H100 scale-ups only when OOM/eviction rates spike beyond 0.5% of sessions for 15 minutes.

3) Fallback & mitigation:
- Immediate: route oversized sessions (predicted >90k tokens) to an H100 pool or to a reduced-sequence fallback model variant.
- Soft degradation: if no H100 capacity available, serve a reduced-context response with a user-facing note (expected for <0.2% of requests).
- Post-incident: automated post-mortem and temporary credits if SLA breach >1hr for p50 during business hours.

4) Cost notes (Ben please expand): expected monthly delta vs A100-only = ~+14–18% for a 20% H100 slice given NovumAI's token mix.

I'll draft a one-page insert for the deal that summarizes these items and include the attachments + simulation graphs. Ben/Kim — can you send the spreadsheet and the canary telemetry thresholds by EOD tomorrow so I can lock the SOW? Liam — appreciate the concurrency numbers; we'll use those for slot-hour modelling.

Best,
Jasmine
